```plato
//==
// # Cloth
//
// The vocabulary cloth simulation needs on top of the deformables already
// declared in `particles.types.plato` (`ClothVertex`, `ClothDistanceConstraint`,
// `ClothBendConstraint`, `Cloth3D`, `Rope3D`). Nothing here re-declares those:
// `Cloth3D` IS the constraint graph, and these types describe where a graph
// comes from, how it is solved, and what it is read back as.
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Building a cloth patch
//  - Solver settings
//  - Cloth bound to a mesh

//==
// # Building a cloth patch
//
// The rectangular lattice a flat cloth patch is built on. Two edge vectors
// rather than a plane and a spacing, so the patch carries its own orientation
// and its own (possibly non-square) cell shape without inventing a convention:
// a vertical curtain is ColumnStep along +X and RowStep along -Z, a tablecloth
// is ColumnStep along +X and RowStep along +Y.
// Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - World space (Z-up, right-handed).

// A grid of ColumnCount by RowCount vertices, vertex (column, row) sitting at
// Origin + column * ColumnStep + row * RowStep. Vertices are numbered in row
// major order, so vertex (column, row) is index row * ColumnCount + column.
// The steps are world displacements in meters; they need not be perpendicular.
type ClothGrid3D
    implements IValue
{
    Origin: Point3D;
    ColumnStep: Vector3D;
    RowStep: Vector3D;
    ColumnCount: Integer;
    RowCount: Integer;
}
```
